description_full: Addus HomeCare Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, provides personal care services to elderly, chronically ill, disabled persons, and individuals who are at risk of hospitalization or institutionalization in the United States. The company operates through three segments: Personal Care, Hospice, and Home Health. Its Personal Care segment provides non-medical assistance with activities of daily living. This segment offers services that include assistance with bathing, grooming, oral care, feeding and dressing, medication reminders, meal planning and preparation, housekeeping, and transportation services. The Hospice segment provides palliative nursing care, social work, spiritual counseling, homemaker, and bereavement counseling services for people who are terminally ill, as well as related services for their families. Its Home Health segment offers skilled nursing and physical, occupational, and speech therapy for the individuals who require assistance during an illness or after hospitalization. The company serves federal, state, and local governmental agencies; managed care organizations; commercial insurers; and private individuals. Addus HomeCare Corporation was founded in 1979 and is based in Frisco, Texas.

financial_summary: Addus HomeCare Corporation is a mid-cap healthcare business with a $2.3B market cap on $1.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +14% over the past three years and +15% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 28%.

The business throws off $104M in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.16× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.8× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 10.2×.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 2.7% of the shares.
